data.content_ref: inline:{"analogy":null,"claim":"As n grows, the probability of reaching unanimous consensus tends to 0. The finite obstruction structures are locally stable mixed configurations in which the crossing edges form a matching: every vertex has at most one opposite-color neighbor, so no vertex flips. The expected number of such stable cuts as a fraction of all two-colorings is exp(-c n), but their basins cover almost all random initial cuts; the final number of crossing edges is \u0398(n) with high probability, so consensus probability vanishes.","counterconditions":[{"case":"If the basin of the empty cut is actually 1-o(1) because stable matching cuts are not reachable from typical initial cuts, then the consensus probability would tend to 1.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"If the final matching size is o(n), then the obstruction prevalence would be sublinear and consensus could tend to 1 or to a constant.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"}],"definitions":[],"derivation":[],"formalization_refs":[],"mechanism":"The number of crossing edges is non-increasing under asynchronous majority updates: a vertex with two opposite neighbors flips and reduces cut size by 1, and a vertex with three opposite neighbors reduces it by 3. Starting from a uniform random cut with about 3n/4 crossing edges, the process descends monotonically to a local minimum. On a random 3-regular graph this zero-temperature Glauber descent jams in a stable matching of crossing edges of linear size; the empty cut's basin is exponentially small, so consensus is not reached whp.","premises":[],"schema":"deepreason-reasoning-envelope-v1","scope":{"covers":[],"excludes":[]},"simulation_refs":[],"uncertainties":[]}
